headline: Sensex Ends Above 81,900 as FII Inflows and Lower Crude Oil Prices Extend Market Gains

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Indian stock markets extended gains for a third straight session supported by foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows.
Softening global crude oil prices helped boost investor sentiment across domestic equities.
Banking stocks led the early morning trade rebound, driving key benchmark indices higher.
Smallcap stocks saw sustained buying, with the NIFTY Smallcap 100 outperforming for a second consecutive session.
whatHappening: NIFTY50 closed around 25,229 while the Sensex ended flat above the 81,900 level.
Life insurance companies registered a 26% rise in new business premium to ₹42,914 crore in October.
Vodafone Idea reported a widened Q2 loss of ₹5,975 crore despite revenue rising 6.2% to ₹11,884 crore.
The Centre received 22 bids under the scheme for 10 GWh giga-scale ACC battery manufacturing capacity.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices extended gains for the third straight day, driven by FII inflows and lower crude oil prices, with Sensex closing above 81,900 and Nifty ending above 25,229.
Nifty Smallcap 100 outperformed for the second consecutive session as broader markets maintained positive momentum.
In corporate developments, Oil India reported more than double net profit, while Vodafone Idea's Q2 net loss widened to ₹5,975 crore.
